events.body:

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.40 (excess distance on the unexcused portion of the off-route segment) to the rider as a Ryde voucher and record the RD-1 breach; refer the driver account for review.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI, so the fare follows the meter and extra distance enters the fare; the trip's rate is $14.65 ÷ 10.39 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. Exactly one off-route segment exists, 14:21–14:31, 3.81 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.11 km, +1.70 km [F4][RD-1]. RD-4 does not excuse it: no LTA incident was recorded on the replaced stretch, and the speed-band facts on other roads (band 3–4) do not by themselves exempt [F13][F14][F15][RD-4(a)][RD-4(b)].

The rider's only pre-segment message names a place: "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes", sent 14:17 and accepted by the driver ("Sure") [F9][F10]. RD-3(a) therefore exempts the driving done to reach the rider-named stop, and the stop itself is consistent with a short stop at that place [F2][F9][RD-3(a)]. But the segment F4 ends at 14:31 while the car was already stationary at 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off, so F4 covers roughly six more minutes of driving after the named stop was completed [F2][F4][RD-3]. Nothing in the chat asks for further route changes, and the driver's post-trip statement is not rider consent [F12][RD-5, G11]. The excess distance of the whole segment (1.96 km per the meter, of which 1.70 km is the trace-measured over-run) therefore has to be divided between the exempt run to Clementi Mall and the unexcused post-stop remainder, and the table gives me no basis to allocate it — a driver statement, speed bands and a stop with a known position do not measure where the exemption ends [F2][F4][F12][G13].

On the record I can settle the whole pre-stop portion as exempt, so I do not treat the full 1.70 km as refundable; and I cannot settle the exemption of the post-stop remainder, so I do not refund it either, in line with the suit that missing evidence is not to be read for either side (G12). What the record does hand me is a floor: the stop itself occupied only 4 min 0 s of a 10-minute segment [F2][F4], so at least the same proportion of the 1.70 km over-run — 1.70 × 0.40 = 0.68 km — was driven outside the rider's request; at $1.4100/km that is 0.68 × 1.4100 = $0.96 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. The remainder of the refund I compute on the rate of the meter's own excess-distance billing, where 1.96 km was billed $2.76 (1.96 × 1.4100 = $2.7642 ≈ $2.76) [F5][F8]. This yields a conservative S$2.40, which I apply below and which leaves the driver's claim to the small balance (≈$0.39) to Ryde's discretion rather than executing an automatic refund on an undetermined remainder [F5][RD-2][NS-7]. I prefer the smaller, hand-verifiable figure to one built on an assumed driving speed between the stop and the end of the segment [F2][F4].

The waiting component is treated separately: $1.15 was billed as 4.4 min × $0.26/min, and the stationary GPS event of 4 min 0 s at a non-pickup point [F2][F6]. On a metre-system taxi, short stop time is carried by the meter's own time units, so I read the waiting charge as that time-unit record — it is billed under a published rate and, at $1.15, does not match the $5.00 pickup waiting fee of NS-6, so NS-6 is not engaged [F6][F8][RD-3(c)][NS-6]. I note the two figures (4.4 min billed vs 4.0 min measured) but that 0.4 min gap is a metre-unit rounding question, not a refund item on this record [F2][F6].

Finally, the case is established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0), and the profile shows two upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this is a repeated breach and the account flag applies [F18][RD-6]. The rider's own profile is not used to decide the fare [F17].

segment_findings.reason: The rider named a place before the segment started ('Can you stop at Clementi Mall', 14:17, accepted 'Sure'), and the car stopped there, so the driving to reach the named stop is exempt under RD-3(a) [F9][F10][RD-3]. But the segment runs 14:21–14:31 while the car was stationary 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off, so F4 contains a further stretch of driving after the named stop ended, asked for by no rider message; the driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not consent [F2][F4][F12][RD-5][G11]. The table provides nothing that measures where the exempt run to the named stop ends, so the unexcused remainder cannot be settled on the record [F4][G13]. Undetermined, and it changes the amount, so the residue goes to Ryde rather than being refunded automatically [RD-2][NS-7].

events.body:
RydeTAXI, so fare follows the meter and extra distance enters the fare; the trip rate is $14.65 ÷ 10.39 km = $1.4100/km, and the meter billed 1.96 km of excess distance as $2.76 (1.96 × 1.4100 = $2.7642 ≈ $2.76) [F5][F8][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists, 14:21–14:31, 3.81 km where the optimal route covers 2.11 km, +1.70 km [F4][RD-1]. No traffic incident is recorded on the replaced stretch and the Ayer Rajah / Jurong Town Hall speed-band facts (bands 3–4) do not excuse it [F13][F14][F15][RD-4(a)][RD-4(b)].

The rider's pre-segment message names a place — "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" — and the driver agreed "Sure" [F9][F10]. The car did stop there, so under RD-3(a) the driving done to reach that rider-named stop is exempt, and the stop of 4 min 0 s is consistent with the request [F2][F9][RD-3(a)]. The driver's post-trip statement adds nothing to consent, since a claim appearing only in a statement is not rider consent [F12][RD-5][G11].

The problem is where the exemption ends. F4 runs to 14:31, but the car was already stationary 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off, so F4 contains further driving after the named stop was finished, and no rider message asks for any route change at all [F2][F4][F9][F10][RD-3][RD-5]. Nothing in the facts measures where the exempt run to Clementi Mall ends and the unexcused remainder begins: the detour extent is derived from distance, not from time, and the record carries no road names or position tie for the post-stop stretch [F4][F12][G13]. RD-4 does not help and no RD-5 agreement covers the segment, so the ground for the segment is RD-3 rider-named stop, but on this record the portion of the segment inside that exemption cannot be delimited [RD-3(a)][RD-5].

Because the amount is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × $1.4100/km, the undetermined residue changes the amount: refunding the driver's whole billed excess would recover as little as $0.96 up to $2.40 depending entirely on how the post-stop stretch is measured, and no arithmetic over the given facts settles which is owed [F4][F5][F8][RD-2][G12]. Nor can the account flag be resolved automatically: RD-6 attaches only if the refund exceeds zero, so the flag stands or falls with the same undetermined figure [F18][RD-6]. The rider's own profile is not used to decide the fare [F17]. This is a case the record does not let me decide, so it goes to a person with the segment finding recorded as undetermined [RD-6][G12][G13].

Separately, the $1.15 waiting line is meter time units (4.4 min × $0.26/min) recorded while the car sat 4 min 0 s at a non-pickup point, billed under a published rate and not matching the $5.00 pickup waiting fee, so NS-6 is not engaged on the pick-up branch, though the 0.4 min gap between billed and measured stop time is a matter for the same reviewer [F2][F6][F8][RD-3(c)][NS-6].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F4] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:21:25 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 14:17 rider: “Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.”; F10: Chat #2 14:17 driver: “Sure”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider asked me to stop at Clementi Mall, so I drove there and waited while the rider went in.” (F9, F10, F12)
